question: A 28-year-old woman with a history of migraines presents to your office due to sudden loss of vision in her left eye and difficulty speaking. Two weeks ago she experienced muscle aches, fever, and cough. Her muscle aches are improving but she continues to have a cough. She also feels as though she has been more tired than usual. She had a similar episode of vision loss 2 years ago and had an MRI at that time. She has a family history of migraines and takes propranolol daily. On swinging light test there is decreased constriction of the left pupil relative to the right pupil. You repeat the MRI and note enhancing lesions in the left optic nerve. Which of the following is used to prevent progression of this condition?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "28-year-old woman with sudden vision loss" -> "history of migraines and recent respiratory symptoms" -> "MRI shows enhancing lesions in left optic nerve" -> "suggestive of optic neuritis" -> "condition may be related to multiple sclerosis" -> "Natalizumab is used to prevent progression of multiple sclerosis" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient presents with vision loss and speech difficulty" -> "previous episode of vision loss and MRI findings" -> "enhancing lesions indicate inflammation" -> "possible demyelinating disease" -> "Natalizumab indicated for treatment of relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Sudden loss of vision and decreased pupil response" -> "MRI reveals lesions in optic nerve" -> "indicates optic neuritis" -> "often associated with multiple sclerosis" -> "Natalizumab is a disease-modifying therapy for MS" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Patient has a history of migraines and recent illness" -> "current symptoms suggest neurological involvement" -> "MRI findings of enhancing lesions" -> "consistent with optic neuritis" -> "Natalizumab is effective in preventing progression" -> 75%
analysis: The patient's symptoms and MRI findings suggest a diagnosis of multiple sclerosis (MS), particularly given the history of vision loss and the presence of enhancing lesions in the optic nerve. Natalizumab is a disease-modifying therapy used to prevent progression of multiple sclerosis and reduce the frequency of relapses. The other options listed (dexamethasone, methotrexate, infliximab, adalimumab) are not typically used for MS management. Therefore, the most appropriate choice for preventing progression in this case is natalizumab.
